Senses.Explanation: The one-color edge is the limit of an undifferentiated, pure-looking field: masters use it for a place an answer or person can reach, inhabit, or become trapped in, and then demand movement beyond it. An unnamed monk calls borrowed expression merely a one-color-edge matter. Xisou Shaotan praises not falling there; Yuanwu Keqin requires personal breakthrough and an encounter even after reaching it. A layman places Xueqiao Yuanxin’s white-on-white image there, and Xueqiao overturns the appraisal. Tianyin Yuanxiu warns that people sit there, while Xueyan Zuqin attacks the claim that snow itself reveals it. The image can mark purity, uniformity, or the absence of visible distinction, but the records repeatedly make that very attainment a possible stopping place. It is therefore not a color description and not an automatic name for completion.
